anya: quick PSA 1: reproduced a steady memory growth on mistral-7b with very long contexts (20k+). seeing paging spikes, eviction churn, and p99 regression after ~15k tokens. details below.

lee: repro steps and env?

anya: headless on dedicated A800, runtime built with newest kernel-selector. run: 
```
./run_infer --model mistral-7b --context 32768 --prompt-file samples/long_stream.txt --batcher continuous --kv-compact-interval 0
```
cold mem: 9.4GB -> after 20k tokens: 11.3GB (+1.9GB)
evictions (kv): ~480 over 20k tokens
page-faults: baseline 1.2k -> 6.9k

carl: do allocator/journal logs show many small free fragments or lots of partially-filled pages?

anya: yes, lots of small free segments. sample allocator snippets: 
```
[12:03:21] kv_alloc page=0x7f9b1d2 size=65536 slots=4 model=mistral-7b mode=GQA
[12:03:27] kv_evict evicted=0x7f9b1d2 reason=oom_estimate last_access=1820 tokens_ago
[12:03:31] kv_alloc page=0x7f9b9ff size=65536 slots=4 model=mistral-7b mode=GQA
[12:03:38] kv_reuse failed_candidate=0x7f9b1d2 frag=true
```

lee: could be MQA/GQA packing mismatch. MQA packs differently so slot alignment changes. If kernel selector falls back to an f16 kernel for long seqs we allocate larger per-slot buffers (more padding) -> higher fragmentation.

anya: selector log shows fallback around 6k tokens: 
```
kernel_select q4_0 not available for seq>2048, fallback -> f16_kernel
```
this lines up with eviction ramp.

carl: also check rope-scaling: different rope_scale changes per-head indexing which can make older pages incompatible for reuse (signature mismatch), causing reuse misses and new allocations.

anya: run had REDWOOD_ROPE_SCALE=1.15. flipping to 1.0 in a quick run reduced evictions ~40%.

perfbot: [auto] profilers uploaded -> /artifacts/1865003210/mistral-kv-profile.tar.gz

lee: what's the micro-batcher behavior? bursts might create short-lived allocations and thrash evictions.

anya: batcher config: 
```
batcher=continuous
min_batch_ms=1
max_batch_ms=50
max_tokens_per_batch=2048
```
clients sending 2-3 concurrent streaming requests cause micro-bursts; pattern is alloc->evict->alloc in tight loop.

carl: mitigation list: 
- prefer q kernels for MQA/GQA compatibility earlier in kernel selector (avoid f16 fallback when q kernel exists but not registered for long seq)
- background kv_compact pass every N tokens to coalesce fragmented slots
- align page sizes to LCM of slot sizes for MQA/GQA to reduce partially-filled pages
- tweak batcher min ms for streaming (raise from 1ms -> 4ms) to smooth bursts

lee: quick experiment idea: enable kv compacting + force rope_scale=1.0 + raise batcher min_ms and run 30k tokens.

anya: ran it. results: 
- evictions down 42%
- mem delta over 30k tokens dropped from +2.7GB -> +0.6GB
- p99 improved 410ms -> 310ms

carl: we should implement a stronger page signature: current signature contains model+head_count only. add rope_scale and qfmt into signature so reuse picks exact matches first. that will cut reuse misses.

lee: small change: extend page metadata to signature_v2 = model|head_count|rope_scale_bin|qfmt. eviction/reuse tries exact match then relaxed. cheap and effective. I can review selector changes.

anya: i'll prototype signature_v2 and add unit tests + bench. will include repro script + logs in PR. recommended runtime flags in PR: 
```
REDWOOD_KV_COMPACT_INTERVAL=5000 \
REDWOOD_ROPE_SCALE=1.0 \
REDWOOD_BATCHER_MIN_MS=4 \
./run_infer --model mistral-7b --context 32768 --prompt-file samples/long_stream.txt
```

infra-bot: note: changing page metadata increases on-disk/persistent footprint on dedicated nodes; ops must be alerted for rollout.

carl: add metric kv_reuse_miss_tagged with reasons (signature_mismatch, frag, pinned) to replace the opaque kv_reuse_fail_count. helps live triage.

lee: agreed. also runtime kernel-team please check selector priority: @lee will own kernel selector pass.

anya: opening PR with prototype + raw logs + artifacts link. thanks all :thumbsup: 

perfbot: created issue GR-6421 "page signature mismatch causing KV fragmentation on long context runs"
